questions.question: Estimate the sum of 4 812 and 3 274 by rounding each number to the nearest thousand. Which estimate is correct?
options: About 8 000
About 7 000
About 8 100
About 9 000
questions.explain: Round each number to the nearest thousand first: 4 812 becomes 5 000 and 3 274 becomes 3 000, so the sum is about 8 000. A common trap is chopping off the digits instead of rounding (4 000 + 3 000 = 7 000), which pulls the estimate too low.

questions.question: Estimate the difference 62 400 minus 28 700 by rounding each number to the nearest ten thousand. Which estimate is correct?
options: About 40 000
About 30 000
About 90 000
About 33 000
questions.explain: To the nearest ten thousand, 62 400 becomes 60 000 and 28 700 becomes 30 000, so the difference is about 30 000. Watch two traps: rounding 28 700 down to 20 000, and adding instead of subtracting, which gives about 90 000.

questions.question: Nina says that 5 940 plus 2 080 is about 8 000. Is her estimate reasonable, and why?
options: Not reasonable — the estimate should be about 10 000
Not reasonable — the estimate should be about 7 000
Reasonable — 5 940 rounds to 6 000 and 2 080 rounds to 2 000, and 6 000 + 2 000 = 8 000
Not reasonable — an estimate must match the exact sum of 8 020
questions.explain: Round each addend to the nearest thousand and add: 6 000 + 2 000 = 8 000, which is very close to the exact sum 8 020. Remember that an estimate is not supposed to equal the exact answer — it only has to be close enough to judge it.

questions.question: Estimate the difference 306 000 minus 149 000 by rounding each number to the nearest ten thousand. Which estimate is correct?
options: About 150 000
About 200 000
About 455 000
About 160 000
questions.explain: To the nearest ten thousand, 306 000 becomes 310 000 and 149 000 becomes 150 000, so the difference is about 160 000 (the exact answer is 157 000). Rounding to the wrong place, such as the nearest hundred thousand, gives 200 000 and is far less accurate.

questions.question: A school in Kelowna collected 4 385 cans in the fall and 5 720 cans in the spring. About how many cans were collected altogether, and why?
options: About 10 000, because 4 385 rounds to 4 000 and 5 720 rounds to 6 000
About 1 000, because 5 720 − 4 385 is about 1 000
questions.explain: Round each number to the nearest thousand — 4 385 goes down to 4 000 and 5 720 goes up to 6 000 — so the total is about 10 000 (the exact total is 10 105). The usual trap is rounding both numbers the same direction, which makes the estimate too low or too high.

questions.question: Liam worked out 70 002 minus 6 985 and wrote the answer 76 987. Use an estimate to judge his answer.
options: Reasonable — 76 987 is close to 70 000, so it makes sense
Not reasonable — 70 000 − 7 000 is about 63 000, so 76 987 is about 14 000 too big; he added instead of subtracting
Not reasonable — the answer should be about 77 000
Reasonable — subtracting across zeros always makes a number larger
questions.explain: Estimate first: 70 000 − 7 000 is about 63 000, so any answer larger than the starting number 70 002 must be wrong (the exact answer is 63 017). Subtraction always makes the number smaller, so an answer that grew is a signal that the numbers were added.

questions.question: A Grade 5 camp needs two tents costing $2 480 and $1 795. The class has a budget of $4 000. Use estimation to decide whether the budget is enough.
options: Yes — the estimate is about $4 000, so it is exactly enough
No — $2 480 rounds to $2 500 and $1 795 rounds to $1 800, so about $4 300 is needed, which is more than $4 000
No — they are about $685 short, because $2 480 − $1 795 is about $685
questions.explain: Round to the nearest hundred and add: 2 500 + 1 800 = 4 300, which is over the $4 000 budget (the exact cost is $4 275). The trap is rounding both prices down to the nearest thousand, which hides the overspending.

questions.question: You want to estimate 27 480 plus 15 260 as closely as possible without adding exactly. Which method gives the estimate closest to the true sum?
options: Round to the nearest thousand: 27 000 + 15 000 = 42 000
Use the benchmarks 25 000 and 15 000: 25 000 + 15 000 = 40 000
Round to the nearest ten thousand: 30 000 + 20 000 = 50 000
Round to the nearest hundred: 27 500 + 15 300 = 42 800
questions.explain: The exact sum is 42 740, and rounding to the nearest hundred lands at 42 800 — only 60 away, because rounding to a smaller place keeps more of each number. Rounding to a big place like the nearest ten thousand is fast but can be thousands off.

questions.question: Priya calculated 500 004 minus 128 736 and got 471 268. Which judgment about her answer is correct?
options: Not reasonable — 500 000 − 130 000 is about 370 000, so her answer is 100 000 too big, likely from not regrouping the hundred thousands
Not reasonable — 500 000 + 130 000 is about 630 000, so her answer is about 160 000 too small, likely from a carry she dropped somewhere
Reasonable — rounding gives 500 000 − 100 000 = 400 000, and 471 268 is near 400 000, so her regrouping across the zeros must be fine
Reasonable — both numbers are large, so a large answer like 471 268 makes sense, and there is no need to estimate any further
questions.explain: Estimate before you trust a long subtraction: 500 000 − 130 000 is about 370 000, and the exact answer is 371 268, so 471 268 is 100 000 too large. Regrouping across the zeros in 500 004 is where this mistake usually happens, and an estimate catches it right away.

questions.question: A BC Ferries route carried 214 800 passengers in July and 268 300 in August. The route record for two months in a row is 500 000 passengers. Without adding exactly, decide whether the record was broken.
options: Yes — 200 000 + 300 000 = 500 000, so the record was matched
No — 210 000 + 270 000 is about 480 000, roughly 20 000 short of the record
No — they are about 53 000 short, because 268 300 − 214 800 is about 53 000
Yes — both months are in the hundred thousands, so the total must be over 500 000
questions.explain: Round each month to the nearest ten thousand and add: 210 000 + 270 000 = 480 000, which is under 500 000 (the exact total is 483 100). Rounding too coarsely, to the nearest hundred thousand, makes the total look like exactly 500 000 and hides the shortfall.

questions.question: Cedar Elementary needs at least $12 000 for a new playground. Donations were $4 780, $3 950 and $2 640. Amrit rounds each to the nearest thousand, gets 5 000 + 4 000 + 3 000 = 12 000, and says the goal is reached. What should you tell him?
options: He is right — the estimate is exactly 12 000, and rounding to the nearest thousand is accurate enough, so the goal is met without adding exactly
He is wrong — rounding down gives 4 000 + 3 000 + 2 000 = 9 000, and rounding down is the safe way to estimate, so they are 3 000 short
He may be wrong — every donation was rounded up, so the estimate is bigger than the real total; adding exactly gives $11 370, short of $12 000
He is right — when an estimate lands on the goal, the goal has always been reached, because rounding errors cancel each other out
questions.explain: When every number is rounded up, the estimate is an overestimate, so it cannot prove a target was reached — here the exact total is $11 370, still $630 short. Whenever an estimate sits right on the goal line, switch to exact addition before deciding.

questions.question: A Tofino campground had 168 400 visitors in 2024 and 191 700 visitors in 2025. A newspaper writes that the campground had nearly half a million visitors over the two years. Is that claim reasonable?
options: Reasonable — rounding each year to the nearest hundred thousand gives 200 000 + 200 000 = 400 000, and 400 000 counts as half a million
Reasonable — 168 400 is almost 200 000 and 191 700 is almost 300 000, so the total is almost 500 000
Not reasonable — the two years differ by only about 20 000, so the total is about 20 000
Not reasonable — rounding to the nearest ten thousand gives 170 000 + 190 000 = 360 000, which is well short of 500 000
questions.explain: Round each year to the nearest ten thousand and add: 170 000 + 190 000 = 360 000, so the exact total of 360 100 is nowhere near half a million (500 000). Be careful not to stretch a number to the next benchmark — 191 700 is close to 200 000, not to 300 000.
